item.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
item.description:
Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets.

By Renato Losio

item.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
item.description:
AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

item.title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
item.description:
Google recently detailed how three interacting bugs across Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Private Service Connect, and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API connectivity failures, blocking around 800 developers from deploying to production.

By Renato Losio
